title: The First Note
subtitle: Start with six cards
story: A restorer finds a note at the bottom of the box. A led the first round. Three cards are already confirmed; recover the other three.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: In round one, A plays ♠5, but B wins. Which card in the pool can beat the spade that was led?

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: With no trumps, only the lead suit can win. B needs a spade higher than 5. Look for the one remaining card that fits.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: B plays ♠9 in round one: it is the only card in the pool that can beat ♠5 in the lead suit. Place it, then use C's failure to follow spades to work out the next round.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠5 → B: ♠9 → C: ♥3. The lead suit is spades. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♥10) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: B: ♥7 → C: ♥10 → A: ♠2. The lead suit is hearts. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: Echoes of a Suit
subtitle: If you have the suit, follow it
story: The second letter includes a scrap of rules. Compare the lead suit with the cards each player uses later, and the gaps begin to narrow.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: C did not follow diamonds in round one. Now look at A's two confirmed slots. Who can still hold the remaining diamond?

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: C played a heart, so C had no diamonds. Both of A's cards are known. The remaining diamond must belong to B, who must follow suit in round one.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: B plays ♦13 in round one. C has no diamonds, and A holds ♦5 and ♠8. Only B can hold ♦13 and must play it when diamonds are led.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♦5 → B: ♦13 → C: ♥9. The lead suit is diamonds. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow diamonds, so the remaining cards (♥2) cannot be diamonds. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: B: ♠3 → C: ♥2 → A: ♠8. The lead suit is spades. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: High Is Not Enough
subtitle: Only the lead suit can win
story: Someone circled a high card without calling it a winner. Outside the lead suit, even the highest rank cannot win the round.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Two ownership clues identify B's entire hand. Decide which suit B must follow before looking for the highest number on the table.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads spades, and B holds a spade. B must play it. Even a higher heart played by C cannot win a round led in spades.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: B plays ♠11 in round one. B holds only ♥3 and ♠11 and must follow spades, so ♥3 cannot be played yet.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠6 → B: ♠11 → C: ♥12. The lead suit is spades. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♥7) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: B: ♥3 → C: ♥7 → A: ♠2. The lead suit is hearts. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: Passing the Lead
subtitle: The winner leads the next round
story: Notes about one round and cards from the next were sealed in separate envelopes. Connect the winner to the next lead to recover the order.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: First find the certain winner of round one. Then use the clue that B wins round two to work backward to its lead suit.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads the highest diamond in the pool, so A will lead round two. To win that round, B must play a higher card of A's suit. Find a remaining pair that works.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♦5 in round one. A wins with ♦13. For B to win round two, A and B must play ♥2 and ♥9 respectively. B did not follow diamonds, and A's hand is full, so ♦5 belongs in C's first round.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♦13 → B: ♠8 → C: ♦5. The lead suit is diamonds. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow diamonds, so the remaining cards (♥9) cannot be diamonds. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: A: ♥2 → B: ♥9 → C: ♠3. The lead suit is hearts. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: The Missing Suit
subtitle: A discard reveals a hand
story: An off-suit card is marked in the margin. Why did its owner not follow suit? Cards played later were still in hand then, leaving a useful trace.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on C's second-round slot. What can B not hold after failing to follow spades? Is A's hand already full?

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: B played a heart in round one and therefore had no spades. A's first spade is fixed and A's other card is known. The remaining spade cannot belong to A or B.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♠2 in round two. B has no spades; A holds ♠11 and ♥3. C already plays ♠6 in round one, leaving ♠2 for C's second round.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠11 → B: ♥7 → C: ♠6. The lead suit is spades. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♥12) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: A: ♥3 → B: ♥12 → C: ♠2. The lead suit is hearts. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: A Third-Round Signature
subtitle: Your first three-round file
story: The last teaching letter adds a third round. Begin with the clearest gap. Swap or undo freely, then replay the result to see how the rounds connect.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: All three cards in round one are visible. Compare the cards of the lead suit to find who leads round two.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: Hearts cannot beat a spade lead. Find the higher of the two spades. Its owner must play the confirmed lead card in round two.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♥3 in round two. C's ♠8 beats A's ♠2, while B's ♥7 cannot win. C therefore leads the confirmed ♥3 in round two.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠2 → B: ♥7 → C: ♠8. The lead suit is spades. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♦5, ♦10) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: C: ♥3 → A: ♥11 → B: ♦5. The lead suit is hearts. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow hearts, so the remaining cards (♦10) cannot be hearts. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: A: ♠12 → B: ♦10 → C: ♠4. The lead suit is spades. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: Raindrops and Tickets
subtitle: Train file 01
story: Rain has blurred the game on the back of a ticket. The conductor saved two opening plays. Recover the cards the passengers had yet to play.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Start with C's third round: two round records and one ownership clue concern this player.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: Each player has exactly three cards, one for each round. If two plays are recorded, another card known to belong to that player must fill the remaining slot.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♣7 in round three. C already plays ♣12 and ♣2 in the first two rounds. The remaining card known to belong to C, ♣7, must fill round three.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♦5 → B: ♦13 → C: ♣12. The lead suit is diamonds. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow diamonds, so the remaining cards (♣2, ♣7) cannot be diamonds. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: B: ♥10 → C: ♣2 → A: ♥4. The lead suit is hearts. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow hearts, so the remaining cards (♣7) cannot be hearts. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: B: ♠3 → C: ♣7 → A: ♠9. The lead suit is spades. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: Carriage Two
subtitle: Train file 02
story: Only two rounds survive from the second carriage. Luggage tags identify some card owners; the remaining gaps must obey the follow-suit rule.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Find the winner of round one, then look for a same-suit pair that lets C win round two.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A's ♠8 is the highest spade, so A leads round two. C must play a higher card of that suit to win. B did not follow spades in round one and cannot hold the other spade.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♠3 in round one. A wins that round. For C to win round two, the only remaining pair is A's ♥2 and C's ♥9. B has no spades and A's hand is full, so ♠3 belongs in C's first round.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠8 → B: ♦13 → C: ♠3. The lead suit is spades. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♦5) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: A: ♥2 → B: ♦5 → C: ♥9. The lead suit is hearts. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: Before the Tunnel
subtitle: Train file 03
story: Before the train entered the tunnel, a clerk recorded the last play they could see. A note about a later winner provides another reliable clue.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on B's slot in round 2. Start with these public records: In round 1, A plays ♣3. In round 1, C plays ♠7. Round 2 is led with ♠4.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♣3 in round one, while C plays ♠7. Players must follow suit, so C had no clubs and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: B plays ♠4 in round two. C did not follow clubs and cannot hold any later. If A won round one with the lowest club, ♣3, B could not hold clubs either. Both remaining clubs would belong to A, who would also need the next lead, ♠4: four cards in a three-card hand. B must instead win round one and lead ♠4.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♣3 → B: ♣13 → C: ♠7. The lead suit is clubs. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow clubs, so the remaining cards (♦11, ♦6) cannot be clubs. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: B: ♠4 → C: ♦11 → A: ♠12. The lead suit is spades. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♦6) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: A: ♣8 → B: ♦2 → C: ♦6. The lead suit is clubs. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: The Window Seat
subtitle: Train file 04
story: A draft carried away half the score sheet, but the players' names remain clear. Combine suit records with card ownership to restore three rounds.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on A's slot in round 2. Start with these public records: In round 1, A plays ♠7. Round 2 is led with ♦5. In round 2, A plays spades.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♠7 in round one, while B plays ♣4. Players must follow suit, so B had no spades and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: A plays ♠3 in round two. A is known to play a spade then, so cannot lead the recorded ♦5. Someone else must have beaten A's ♠7 in round one. Only ♠12 can do that, leaving ♠3 as A's second-round spade.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠7 → B: ♣4 → C: ♠12. The lead suit is spades. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♦10, ♦2) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: C: ♦5 → A: ♠3 → B: ♦10. The lead suit is diamonds. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

A did not follow diamonds, so the remaining cards (♣13) cannot be diamonds. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: B: ♦2 → C: ♣8 → A: ♣13. The lead suit is diamonds. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: Tea in the Dining Car
subtitle: Train file 05
story: A tea stain covers the ranks. The clerk copied the suits elsewhere, and the porter confirmed who originally held several cards.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on C's slot in round 1. Start with these public records: In round 1, A plays ♠3. C originally holds ♣2. C originally holds ♠7.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♠3 in round one, while B plays ♣11. Players must follow suit, so B had no spades and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♠7 in round one. C's entire hand is ♣2 and ♠7. A has led spades, so C must follow with ♠7 rather than play the club.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠3 → B: ♣11 → C: ♠7. The lead suit is spades. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♣6) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: C: ♣2 → A: ♠12 → B: ♣6. The lead suit is clubs. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: After the Junction
subtitle: Train file 06
story: The jolt at a junction scattered the handwriting. The first card survives. Every later lead still belongs to the previous round's winner.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on C's slot in round 2. Start with these public records: In round 1, A plays ♠3. In round 1, B plays ♥5. Round 2 is led with ♠9.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♠3 in round one, while B plays ♥5. Players must follow suit, so B had no spades and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♠9 in round two. B did not follow spades and holds none. If C also failed to follow, all three remaining spades would belong to A. With the already played ♠3, that would give A four cards instead of three. C must win round one with a higher spade and lead ♠9 next.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠3 → B: ♥5 → C: ♠6. The lead suit is spades. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♥2, ♥14) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: C: ♠9 → A: ♠13 → B: ♥2. The lead suit is spades. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♥14) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: A: ♣7 → B: ♥14 → C: ♥10. The lead suit is clubs. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: The Night Conductor
subtitle: Train file 07
story: The night conductor missed some cards but left a check beside a winner. That mark is as reliable as the limit on each player's hand.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on C's slot in round 1. Start with these public records: In round 1, A plays ♠5. In round 1, B plays ♥12. Round 2 is led with ♦9. B wins round 3.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♠5 in round one, while B plays ♥12. Players must follow suit, so B had no spades and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♠13 in round one. B has no spades, so ♠13 belongs to A or C. If A kept it while winning with ♠5, A would then lead ♦9, the highest diamond, and lead ♠13 in round three. B, with no spades, could not win that round. This contradicts the reliable winner record. C must play ♠13 in round one.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠5 → B: ♥12 → C: ♠13. The lead suit is spades. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♣4, ♥7) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: C: ♦9 → A: ♦3 → B: ♣4. The lead suit is diamonds. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow diamonds, so the remaining cards (♥7) cannot be diamonds. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: C: ♥2 → A: ♣10 → B: ♥7. The lead suit is hearts. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: The Folded Timetable
subtitle: Train file 08
story: A line is missing along the timetable's fold. Later plays can still prove which players could not have held the missing card.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on A's slot in round 2. Start with these public records: In round 1, A plays ♣10. Round 2 is led with ♦14.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♣10 in round one, while B plays ♦2. Players must follow suit, so B had no clubs and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: A plays ♦14 in round two. A's opening ♣10 is the highest club in the pool and cannot lose to another suit. A wins round one and must lead the confirmed ♦14 next.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♣10 → B: ♦2 → C: ♣4. The lead suit is clubs. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow clubs, so the remaining cards (♦5, ♦11) cannot be clubs. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: A: ♦14 → B: ♦5 → C: ♠6. The lead suit is diamonds. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow diamonds, so the remaining cards (♠12) cannot be diamonds. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: A: ♦8 → B: ♦11 → C: ♠12. The lead suit is diamonds. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: A Call from the Platform
subtitle: Train file 09
story: A call from the platform adds one definite record. Check it against the carriage notes, remembering that no card can appear twice.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on B's slot in round 2. Start with these public records: In round 1, A plays ♠2. In round 1, C plays ♦12. Round 2 is led with ♥3.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♠2 in round one, while C plays ♦12. Players must follow suit, so C had no spades and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: B plays ♥3 in round two. C did not follow spades and cannot hold any remaining spade. If B also failed to follow, A would hold all three spades. A would win, but have no room in hand for the next lead, ♥3. B must win with a higher spade and then lead ♥3.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠2 → B: ♠11 → C: ♦12. The lead suit is spades. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♥8, ♦7) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: B: ♥3 → C: ♥8 → A: ♠6. The lead suit is hearts. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

A did not follow hearts, so the remaining cards (♦4) cannot be hearts. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: C: ♦7 → A: ♦4 → B: ♥13. The lead suit is diamonds. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: A Minute in the Dark
subtitle: Train file 10
story: The lights went out, but play continued around the same seats. Each name still marks the same column; only the leader may change.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on A's slot in round 2. Start with these public records: In round 1, A plays ♠10. Round 2 is led with ♦3.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♠10 in round one, while C plays ♥4. Players must follow suit, so C had no spades and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: A plays ♦3 in round two. A's opening ♠10 is the highest spade in this game, so A wins round one. The winner leads next, placing the confirmed ♦3 in A's second-round slot.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♠10 → B: ♠5 → C: ♥4. The lead suit is spades. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow spades, so the remaining cards (♦12, ♦7) cannot be spades. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: A: ♦3 → B: ♥13 → C: ♦12. The lead suit is diamonds. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow diamonds, so the remaining cards (♥8) cannot be diamonds. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: C: ♦7 → A: ♠2 → B: ♥8. The lead suit is diamonds. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: Three Rounds to Go
subtitle: Train file 11
story: Near the terminus, three passengers played out their hands. Amid the mixed suits, the cards they could not follow offer valuable evidence.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on A's slot in round 2. Start with these public records: In round 1, B plays ♦7. Round 2 is led with ♥4. In round 1, C plays ♦3.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♣5 in round one, while B plays ♦7. Players must follow suit, so B had no clubs and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: A plays ♥4 in round two. B and C play ♦7 and ♦3 in round one. If A leads diamonds, only the higher ♦11 remains. If A leads another suit, neither B nor C can win. Either way, A wins and leads ♥4 in round two.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♣5 → B: ♦7 → C: ♦3. The lead suit is clubs. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow clubs, so the remaining cards (♥12, ♥2) cannot be clubs. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

C did not follow clubs, so the remaining cards (♥8, ♦11) cannot be clubs. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: A: ♥4 → B: ♥12 → C: ♥8. The lead suit is hearts. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

Round 3: B: ♥2 → C: ♦11 → A: ♣10. The lead suit is hearts. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: The Last Train Filed
subtitle: Train file 12
story: All twelve pages have arrived. Check ownership, winners, and remaining hands together to bring this journey to a complete close.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on C's slot in round 1. Start with these public records: In round 1, A plays ♦6. Round 2 is led with ♣5. In round 2, C plays ♦9.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: A leads ♦6 in round one, while B plays ♣10. Players must follow suit, so B had no diamonds and cannot play that suit in a later round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♦3 in round one. C still holds ♦9 for round two and must follow A's diamond lead. ♦9 cannot be used early, leaving ♦3 or ♦13. If C won with ♦13, C would have to lead ♣5 next, contradicting the confirmed ♦9. Only ♦3 works.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: A: ♦6 → B: ♣10 → C: ♦3. The lead suit is diamonds. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

B did not follow diamonds, so the remaining cards (♣14, ♣2) cannot be diamonds. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: A: ♣5 → B: ♣14 → C: ♦9. The lead suit is clubs. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow clubs, so the remaining cards (♦13) cannot be clubs. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: B: ♣2 → C: ♦13 → A: ♥7. The lead suit is clubs. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: Before the Chime
subtitle: Tea room file 01
story: Three rounds were recorded before the clock chimed. The notes are now out of order. Use the lead cards and winners to reconnect them.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on C's slot in round 1. Start with these public records: In round 1, C plays spades. In round 3, C plays ♠10.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: Place the known suits and cards with their players and rounds. Each card is used once. A card played in a later round was still in that player's hand earlier and was subject to the follow-suit rule.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: C plays ♠4 in round one. There are only two spades: ♠4 and ♠10. C must play a spade in round one, but ♠10 is reserved for C's third round. A card cannot be used twice, so ♠4 is the only choice.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: B: ♣5 → C: ♠4 → A: ♣8. The lead suit is clubs. A holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow clubs, so the remaining cards (♥6, ♠10) cannot be clubs. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: A: ♣2 → B: ♣11 → C: ♥6. The lead suit is clubs. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

C did not follow clubs, so the remaining cards (♠10) cannot be clubs. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 3: B: ♣14 → C: ♠10 → A: ♥12. The lead suit is clubs. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: A Misplaced Coaster
subtitle: Tea room file 02
story: A lead-card record lies beneath a coaster. The coaster's position proves nothing about the seats; rely on the named records and the rules.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on A's slot in round 1. Start with these public records: A originally holds ♦5. In round 2, A plays ♦13.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: ♦5 must go in A's column. Each player has exactly 2 cards. If you place it in a later round, check whether that would mean failing to follow its suit in an earlier round.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: A plays ♦5 in round one. A is known to hold ♦5 and to play ♦13 in round two. With exactly two cards per player, ♦5 must occupy A's first round.

authorSolution.explanation:
Round 1: C: ♥2 → A: ♦5 → B: ♥9. The lead suit is hearts. B holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

A did not follow hearts, so the remaining cards (♦13) cannot be hearts. This follows from the requirement to follow suit when able.

Round 2: B: ♠3 → C: ♠8 → A: ♦13. The lead suit is spades. C holds the highest card of that suit and wins.

title: Beginning with B
subtitle: Tea room file 03
story: B leads this game. The seats still cycle A, B, C, and each new round starts with the previous winner.

hints.title: Look at the evidence
hints.text: Focus on B's slot in round 2. Start with these public records: Round 2 is led with ♦13. Round 1 is led with ♦8.

hints.title: Connect the rules
hints.text: ♦13 is the first card of round 2, so only that round's leader can play it. Connect this to the previous winner, then check the same-suit cards still in each hand.

hints.title: One step forward
hints.text: B plays ♦13 in round two. B opens with ♦8. The only higher diamond, ♦13, is reserved as the next round's lead, so nothing can beat ♦8 in round one. B wins and then leads ♦13.

authorSolution.explanation:
